issues.issue: Does Guideline 7 breach procedural fairness on its face (the cross-appeal)?
issues.applicant_position: Guideline 7 is not unfair on its face; fairness may require exceptions, as the Minister conceded (para 10).
issues.respondent_position: Guideline 7 denies claimants a fair hearing by barring questioning first by their own counsel (para 3).
issues.result_quote: the procedure prescribed by Guideline 7 is not, on its face, in breach of the Board’s duty of fairness.

issues.issue: Does Guideline 7 unlawfully fetter RPD members' discretion over the order of questioning?
issues.applicant_position: Guideline 7 leaves members free to depart in exceptional circumstances; the Federal Court wrongly found a fetter (para 5).
issues.respondent_position: Guideline 7's mandatory language unlawfully fetters members' discretion over the order of questioning (paras 3, 5).
issues.result_quote: Guideline 7 is not an unlawful fetter on the exercise of members’ discretion on the conduct of refugee protection hearings.

issues.issue: Is Guideline 7 invalid because it changes procedure and should have been a rule under s.161(1)(a)?
issues.applicant_position: Guideline 7 is valid as a guideline; the Chairperson could choose that instrument (paras 90-108).
issues.respondent_position: Guideline 7 is a rule of procedure that should have gone through s.161(1)(a) with Cabinet approval (para 94).
issues.result_quote: it was not unreasonable for the Chairperson to choose to implement the standard order of questioning through the more flexible legislative instrument

issues.issue: Must a fetter finding always lead to granting judicial review (third certified question)?
issues.result_quote: the third question does not arise and need not be answered.
